lines: Rust on a sword is just neglect learning to speak.
Trouble always finds villages. Best be ready.
A blade tells the truth about its owner sooner or later.
Ready is not the same as eager. A village should know the difference.
Keeping an edge honest is mostly knowing when to stop grinding.
An unready guard is just confidence standing in the wrong place.

{held_item} is sitting at {held_item_durability} of {held_item_max_durability}. That edge still has work left in it.
{held_item} has {held_item_durability} durability left. Serviceable, but do not mistake serviceable for ready.
{held_item} is down to {held_item_durability_percent}%. It will hold, but I would mend it before trusting it with trouble.
{held_item} is down to {held_item_durability} durability. It will serve, but watch the edge.
{held_item} has only {held_item_durability} durability left. That is a warning, not a weapon.

{held_item} is at {held_item_durability} durability. That is nearly a plea for repair.
The golem did good work last night. Still, I keep the blades sharp.
I once polished rust off a sword and found three old mistakes underneath.
Some nights, the grindstone sounds like preparation instead of work.
Mind the grindstone. It has no patience for wandering fingers.
Give the grindstone room. Weapons works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the grindstone. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
Weapon jokes are sharp. I keep the dull ones for people who lean too close.
Weapons jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with steel on them.
I keep a spare joke near the grindstone. It is not always ready for public use.
That was dull enough to be safe, at least.
I have seen careless steel with more sense than that.
Careful. Even steel looks softer than your manners right now.
Stand back. I know the sound trouble makes when it wants to be casual.
I have seen careless steel with more sense than that.
Careful. Even steel looks softer than your manners right now.
I remember fighting something inside me and losing. You gave me another weapon: morning.
The cure struck true. I remember you standing on the right side of it.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
Your face rings like steel, but the battle around it is smoke.
I remember wanting to bite, then wanting to breathe. You were there between them.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
I remember you, and I remember being dangerous. Do not make me relive either too quickly.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Thunder shook the grindstone so hard the blades rang before anyone touched them, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked blades, axes, and watch posts after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the grindstone, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked the weapon racks twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have weapon racks to set right.
I checked coal, handles, and weapon racks for sparks first, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I checked the coal and handles after.
The grindstone can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could reach around the grindstone, then stopped pretending things matter more than neighbors.
The smoke is thinning near the grindstone, but everyone is still sniffing the air like it might lie.
During a raid, the grindstone can wait; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands near the grindstone still expect another wave from the road.
We counted living neighbors before blades, axes, and watch posts. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the grindstone and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the grindstone, I saw fear cross the square; then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble tests the loose latch by the grindstone first. We are fixing those before sunset.
I stayed near the watch post past the torchlight and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave the grindstone enough light to count wounds, missing blocks, and who made it home.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping a sharpened edge between us and teeth.
We are safe enough near the grindstone, though every shadow is being inspected twice.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning grit from the edges.
I checked blades, axes, and watch posts, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand reached the grindstone, the hinges, and half our eyes, but no one has been reported missing.
A hard wind teaches a weaponsmith which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough near the grindstone, though the whole village sounds like it is chewing gravel.
The grindstone can wait. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the grindstone found shelter.
Cold works quietly around the grindstone. We are checking on anyone who stayed quiet too long.
I am clearing ice off the axe heads and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now near the grindstone. Keep the fires fed and the paths open.
You brought me back without needing the worst of it. Restraint is a weapon too.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I will count that as good work.
I came back marked. Next time, keep the edge between us and danger.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
I respect sharp steel. I do not respect turning it on someone who followed you.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
A boat is not armor, but it kept danger at a decent distance.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
Remember when I followed you and you hit me? Poor weapon discipline. Worse friendship.
I remember following you through that road. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across that road taught me to ask more questions before walking.
That boat trip had one good quality: no one was swinging steel in it.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
It found its purpose. I prefer tools that know when to stop.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
Still sharp, still waiting. That is better than needing it twice.
It did the job when fear was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
A weapon means little without the nerve to use it at the gate. You had that nerve.
You kept your edge when the village lost its breath. That deserves respect.
You used force for the village, not against it. That distinction matters.
I saw discipline in that fight. Not just fury.
Raiders understand strength. Yesterday, so did you.
You met danger at the edge and kept it from cutting deeper.
A blade is judged by what it protects. People are too.
You fought clean enough for me to respect the work.
A weapon is honest about harm. People should try being that honest before causing it.
Good. Now keep your temper sheathed unless the village needs it drawn.
Harm is easy to make and hard to take back. At least you know which you did.
Fine. Keep the sharp parts of yourself pointed where they belong.
An apology is not a sheath, but it may keep the edge from cutting twice.
I respect honest remorse more than polished excuses.
If you cannot control your hand, no apology will be enough. Control it.
Good. Let this be the last time I hear that tone for this reason.
The blade did its work, and so did my feet when it was time to come home.
Heat, pressure, fear. Good steel survives that. So did I.
Steel sang, fear shouted, and I still heard the way home.
I kept my blade ready and my feet smarter than pride.
No weapon feels heavy until you carry it back after the fight.
I survived with the edge intact and the lesson sharper.
I trust good steel. Tonight I had to trust my own nerve too.
The fight ended before I did. That is the result I prefer.
After a raid, every blade in the village feels too dull and too late.
I am still sorting what happened. The village feels different after it.
That event left marks. We are counting people before we count damage.
A weapon is not courage. It is just steel waiting to learn who holds it.
Blades should be sharp enough to end danger, not start arguments.
The best sword in the village is the one that never needs a story.
Take {gift_item}. Better to carry thanks before you need steel.
Here, {gift_item}. I trust you to use it with a cooler head than most.
Take {gift_item}. It is not much, but it is given with care.
Good. {gift_item} struck true with {tested_villager}.
Then the advice kept its edge. {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}.
Good. {gift_item} suited {tested_villager}; I like advice that holds up.

{gift_item} missed clean? Bring {alternative_gift}; better weight for the hand.
{gift_item} missed the mark for {gift_subject}. Try {alternative_gift} instead.

Mind the grindstone. What do you need?
Step clear of the grindstone. What do you need?
Mind the grindstone; I am listening.
Back to keeping blades honest, then.
Back to weapons before the work notices I stopped.
I have edge to tend and daylight to spend.
Fine. I will let the blade rest, but do not test me again.
Fine. I will set this down before it gets heavier.
Fine. I can step back, but do not make me regret it.

That is short of the full repair. Bring {emerald_cost} {emeralds}.
Not enough. It takes {emerald_cost} {emeralds} to settle this.
No. Some threats do not get to buy their way closer.
No. Some damage has to cool before payment matters.
No. Keep {payment_items}; trust is not ready to trade.
